newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bavaria October CPI up 1.4 percent year-on-year.
newsitem.headline: Bavaria October CPI up 1.4 percent year-on-year.

text.p: The statistics office for the German state of Bavaria said on Thursday that consumer prices in October were unchanged month-on-month, and increased by 1.4 percent compared to a year ago.
The previous month prices fell 0.1 percent month-on-month and grew 1.3 percent on the previous year.

Earlier, the state statistics office in Hesse said consumer prices rose 1.3 percent year-on-year and were unchanged month-on-month in October, compared with September's 1.2 percent and one percent drop respectively.

Later, the southern state of Baden-Wuerttemberg said prices were unchanged on the month and up 1.3 percent on the year, compared with a drop of 0.2 percent on the month and an increase of 1.2 percent year-on-year in September.
This was followed by consumer prices data from North Rhine-Westphalia, where prices grew 0.1 percent month-on-month and 1.5 percent on an annual basis.
